extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff and counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Final order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state-court suspension; it sets suspension/probation, describes notice/publication/reinstatement procedures, and prescribes administrative measures (Customer Numbers, PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action may be imposed by the USPTO pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order was predicated upon Respondent being suspended from the practice of law by the Supreme Court of California (In re Jens Edward Hoekendijk). The Office acts pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (timing and delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must mail a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' to the respondent and provide an opportunity to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. provided). The response window is 40 days and the respondent may oppose imposition of identical discipline based on reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of respondent's non-opposition on factual dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not oppose the imposition of reciprocal discipline, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and identical discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's statement that he 'does not oppose the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the California Supreme Court' was taken as eliminating a genuine factual dispute and supported summary imposition of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may impose discipline identical to that imposed by the state authority (e.g., suspension for one year, stayed/specified probation, initial shorter suspension period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, the Office ordered suspension for one year, placement on one year probation, and permitted reinstatement application after completing thirty (30) days of the USPTO suspension, mirroring the California order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing a specified portion of the suspension (here thirty (30) days), the respondent may seek reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent is reinstated during his probationary period, he will be permitted to practice patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the USPTO during the remainder of his probationary period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette and OED public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette and disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the specific text of the Notice of Suspension for publication and states that disciplinary decisions are posted at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and public under § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures cross-jurisdictional notification of the discipline and its grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of a suspended practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent who is suspended must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires Respondent shall comply with § 11.58 duties (the Order does not reproduce § 11.58; consulte the regulation for specifics, e.g., client notification, return of files, cessation of practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative measures: dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order also prohibits the respondent from applying for, obtaining, or having his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO; these measures affect electronic filing/access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or holding Customer Numbers during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall his name be added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative administrative restriction imposed during suspension to prevent use of USPTO electronic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary basis: moral turpitude/dishonesty (example conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: State discipline may be predicated on findings of moral turpitude, dishonesty, and corruption — e.g., intentionally reporting compliance with MCLE requirements when knowing one was not in compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The California Supreme Court found Respondent intentionally committed an act of moral turpitude and willful violation of California Business and Professions Code § 6106 by falsely reporting MCLE compliance; such conduct supports reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of practice restrictions while disciplined before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension/probation applies to practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states the respondent is suspended 'from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO' for the period of suspension/probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for posting and taking action (statutory/regulatory citation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (and related provisions § 11.58, § 11.59, § 11.60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these statutes/regulations as the basis for the imposition, publication, notification, duties, and reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad remedial/reservations clause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order reserves 'such other and further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows the Office to impose additional measures as necessary beyond the specifically listed remedies.
